graph_recc_sys.engine module

class graph_recc_sys.engine.NeuralNetworkEngine(loader: GraphLoader, hyperparams: HyperParams)[source]

Bases: object

Coordinate training, validation, test-time evaluation, inference, and prediction post-processing for a graph-based neural recommendation engine.

This class acts as the high-level orchestration component of the recommendation pipeline. It receives subgraphs, loaders, and label indices from a GraphLoader instance and delegates the actual operations to specialized training, inference, and evaluation components.

The engine supports multiple training modes, handles optimization utilities such as optimizer, learning-rate scheduler, and warmup, logs experiments and checkpoints through MLflow, and provides utility methods to decode and export generated recommendations.

training(model: Module, dry_run: bool, device: device, run_name: str)[source]

Train the model, run validation at each epoch, and log metrics and checkpoints to MLflow.

Depending on the configured loss function, the engine automatically switches between: - triplet mode for metric-learning / contrastive losses - binary mode for edge classification losses

Supported loss functions: - TripletMarginLoss - BPRLoss - InfoNCE - MultiLoss - BCEWithLogitsLoss - FocalLoss

Parameters:

  • model (Module) – PyTorch model to train.

  • dry_run (bool) – If True, no artifacts or metrics are logged to MLflow.

  • device (device) – PyTorch device used for training and validation.

  • run_name (str) – Name of the MLflow run.

Return type:

None

Returns:

None

Raises:

  • ValueError – If self.params.loss_function is invalid.

  • ValueError – If self.params.mode becomes invalid during training.

give_prediction(pred_index_mat: Tensor, item_inv_map: dict[int, Any], user_inv_map: dict[int, Any], product_names_path: str | Path, user_idx_list: list[int] | Tensor | None = None, edge_label_index: EdgeIndex | Tensor | None = None, pretty_print: bool = False, dump: bool = False, dir: str | Path | None = None)[source]

Decode model predictions into original customer/product identifiers and, if provided, attach the products actually purchased in the ground truth.

If dump=True, the method also exports the recommendations to a CSV file.

Output structure:
{
customer_id: {
“bought”: {

product_id: product_name, …

}, “recommended”: {

product_id: product_name, …

}

}

Parameters:

  • pred_index_mat (Tensor) – Matrix of predicted item indices with shape (n_users, k).

  • item_inv_map (dict[int, Any]) – Reverse mapping from internal item indices to original product ids.

  • user_inv_map (dict[int, Any]) – Reverse mapping from internal user indices to original customer ids.

  • product_names_path (str | Path) – Path to the CSV file containing product ids and product names.

  • user_idx_list (list[int] | Tensor | None) – Optional list of global user indices corresponding to the rows of pred_index_mat. If None, row indices are treated as global ids.

  • edge_label_index (EdgeIndex | Tensor | None) – Optional ground-truth user-item edges to attach as “bought”.

  • pretty_print (bool) – If True, print the decoded output as formatted JSON.

  • dump (bool) – If True, export recommendations to CSV.

  • dir (str | Path | None) – Output CSV path used when dump=True.

Returns:

Nested dictionary containing bought and recommended products for each customer.

Return type:

dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, str | None]]]

Raises:

  • ValueError – If dump=True and no output path is provided.

  • KeyError – If a predicted user or item index is not found in the provided inverse mappings.

class graph_recc_sys.extraction.DatasetManager(hyperparams: Any | None = None)[source]

Bases: object

Manage dataset extraction and local persistence for training data, recommendation tables, and analysis tables.

Training datasets and recommendation tables are defined consistently from the provided hyperparameters, while analysis tables are downloaded through a separate flow.

Expected directory structure:

class graph_recc_sys.graph_dataset.MarketBasketGraphBuilder(dataset_manager: DatasetManager)[source]

Bases: DataClass, InMemoryDataset

Build and manage a PyTorch Geometric heterogeneous graph from market basket, product master data, and customer master data.

This class: - reads the input CSV files - preprocesses the source tables - builds a heterogeneous user-item graph - attaches node features for users and products - saves the processed graph to disk - saves and reloads the mappings between original ids and internal indices

The resulting graph contains: - user nodes - product nodes - edges between users and products representing purchase interactions - edge timestamps for possible temporal splits - numerical node features for both users and products

graph_recc_sys.graph_loader module

class graph_recc_sys.graph_loader.GraphLoader(data: HeteroData, hyperparams)[source]

Bases: DataClass

Utility class for building temporal train/validation/test splits and corresponding PyG loaders for link prediction on a heterogeneous user-item graph.

The class sorts interactions by time, creates temporal edge splits, builds subgraphs containing only the allowed context edges for each phase, and instantiates LinkNeighborLoader objects for training and validation.

It also prepares: - edge label indices for training, validation, and test - exclusion links for validation and test, used to filter out already-seen

interactions from recommendation candidates

The split strategy is temporal: - training targets come from the earliest interactions - validation targets come after training - test targets come after validation - validation and test context only include training edges

Parameters:

  • data (HeteroData) – Input heterogeneous graph containing user-item interactions and timestamps.

  • hyperparams – Configuration object containing batching and neighborhood sampling hyperparameters.

graph_recc_sys.neural_network module

class graph_recc_sys.neural_network.RecommenderModel(data: HeteroData, hyperparams)[source]

Bases: Module, DataClass

Neural model for link prediction on a heterogeneous user-item graph.

The model builds initial user and item node representations either from learnable free embeddings or from available node features through embedding/linear transformations. These representations are then propagated through a stack of heterogeneous GraphSAGE convolution layers and finally projected into a latent output space.

In binary mode, the decoder produces a score for each candidate edge using the dot product between user and item embeddings. In triplet mode, the model directly returns normalized node embeddings, which can be used with metric-learning or contrastive objectives.

Parameters:

  • data (HeteroData) – Heterogeneous graph containing nodes, node features, and edges.

  • hyperparams – Configuration object containing all model hyperparameters.

Hyperparameters:
n_conv_layer (int):

Number of heterogeneous convolution layers.

n_projs_layer (int):

Number of hidden projection layers before the final output layer.

dropout_rate (float):

Dropout rate applied after convolutions and projection layers.

input_channels (int):

Dimension of the initial node representations.

hidden_channels (int):

Dimension of the hidden representations after graph convolutions.

out_channels (int):

Final latent embedding dimension.

mode (str):

Output mode of the model. Supported values: “binary” or “triplet”.

two_tower (bool):

If True, uses separate projection heads for users and items. Otherwise, a shared projection head is used.

proj_norm (str | None):

Normalization type used in projection layers. Supported values: “LayerNorm”, “BatchNorm”, or None.

aggr (str):

Aggregation strategy used inside SAGEConv.

add_features (bool):

If True, initial node representations are built from node features. If False, free embeddings are used for users and items.

num_stochastic_item_features (int):

Number of additional free embedding components concatenated to item representations when add_features=True.

num_stochastic_user_features (int):

Number of additional free embedding components concatenated to user representations when add_features=True.
